title: Channel-wise Vector Quantization: Native 1D Visual Tokenization with Learnable Ordering
claim: Prior methods tokenize and generate in a 2D patch raster order; ours uses ordered channel tokens, producing a coarse-to-fine sequence.
layout: 2 halves split by dashed line; left tokenizer diagrams, right stacked sample rows
description: The figure is split by a vertical dashed line. On the left, a 3D feature cube labeled h, w, c branches into two arrows. Arrow (a) VQ leads to a grid of 2D tokens with index numbers and a raster-scan arrow, plus a VQ codebook of ID and embedding rows with c-length bars. Arrow (b) CVQ leads to stacked colored channel slices that form a natively 1D index sequence, plus a CVQ codebook of h×w slabs. On the right, two rows of images are headed by blue arrows. The top row, 'Traditional AR: next-patch prediction in 2D raster-scan order', shows an apple painted from top to bottom. Below it, 'CAR (ours)' shows 8 to 256 tokens, with apple, cat, and salad images going from blurry to sharp. The eye goes first to the sample grids.
caption: (Left) VQ vs. CVQ. Conventional VQ assigns an index to each 1×1×c patch feature vector, while CVQ assigns an index to each channel of the feature map. (Right) AR vs. CAR. Traditional autoregressive (AR) models generate images patch by patch in raster scan order (here, Emu3 [42]), whereas our channel-wise autoregressive (CAR) model generates images channel by channel in a 1D coarse-to-fine order. For example, given the prompt “a photo of an apple”, the model first sketches a red circular shape corresponding to the apple’s outline and dominant color, then progressively depicts its appearance, and finally adds fine-grained details such as specular highlights and yellow speckles.
abstract: We present Channel-wise Vector Quantization (CVQ), a novel image tokenization paradigm that replaces patch-wise tokens with channel-wise tokens. Unlike conventional vector quantization, which assigns a discrete token to each patch feature vector, CVQ quantizes each channel of the feature map. This represents an image as a 1D channel sequence with learnable coarse-to-fine ordering, rather than a 2D patch grid. Based on CVQ, we introduce a new visual autoregressive framework with "next-channel prediction". Instead of rendering images patch by patch in raster order, our Channel-wise Autoregressive (CAR) model predicts image channels sequentially, producing progressively enriched visual details. Specifically, it first sketches global structure and then refines fine-grained attributes, akin to a human artist's workflow. Empirically, we show that: (1) CVQ exhibits strong codebook scalability, maintaining 95%+ utilization with up to $2^{16}$ entries while delivering growing reconstruction gains over VQ as the codebook scales up; and (2) CAR attains a DPG score of 86.7 and a GenEval score of 0.79, demonstrating strong effectiveness for text-to-image generation.
